questions.stem: This question is about magnesium metal and its compounds.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The diagram represents the structure of magnesium. Complete the diagram by adding the labels.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Explain why magnesium is malleable.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Magnesium burns in oxygen gas to form solid magnesium oxide.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Complete the chemical equation for the reaction by balancing the equation and adding the state symbols. $\mathrm {M g (s)} + \mathrm {O} _ {2} (\mathrm {)} \rightarrow \mathrm {M g O} (\mathrm {})$

parts.label: b-ii

parts.label: c
parts.text: A student uses this method to make a solution of magnesium chloride. Step 1 measure $ 2 5 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of dilute hydrochloric acid into a beaker Step 2 add magnesium powder a little at a time Step 3 keep adding magnesium powder until it is in excess Step 4 remove the excess magnesium powder by filtration This is the equation for the reaction. $\mathrm {M g} (\mathrm {s}) + 2 \mathrm {H C l} (\mathrm {a q}) \rightarrow \mathrm {M g C l} _ {2} (\mathrm {a q}) + \mathrm {H} _ {2} (\mathrm {g})$

parts.label: c-i

parts.label: c-ii

questions.stem: This question is about the manufacture of ethanol by the fermentation of glucose.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Fermentation needs to be done in the absence of air. Give two other conditions needed for fermentation.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why fermentation needs to be done in the absence of air.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Complete the equation for fermentation. $\mathrm {C} _ {6} \mathrm {H} _ {1 2} \mathrm {O} _ {6} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm {C} _ {2} \mathrm {H} _ {5} \mathrm {O H} + 2.$

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: A mixture containing 500 mol of glucose is fermented. A mass of 5750 g of ethanol is obtained. Calculate the percentage yield. [for ethanol, $ M_{r}=4 6 $]

questions.stem: Sodium sulfate can be prepared by the reaction between sodium hydroxide solution and sodium hydrogensulfate $ \mathrm{(N a H S O_{4})} $ solution. This is the equation for the reaction. $\mathrm {N a O H} (\mathrm {a q}) + \mathrm {N a H S O} _ {4} (\mathrm {a q}) \rightarrow \mathrm {N a} _ {2} \mathrm {S O} _ {4} (\mathrm {a q}) + \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O} (\mathrm {I})$ Sodium hydrogensulfate solution is acidic. The student does a titration. A student adds $ 2 5. 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of sodium hydroxide solution to a conical flask and adds two drops of indicator.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name a piece of apparatus that should be used to add $ 2 5. 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of sodium hydroxide solution to the conical flask.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Describe the method the student should use to find the accurate volume of sodium hydrogensulfate solution needed to neutralise the $ 2 5. 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of sodium hydroxide solution.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The student repeats the titration without the indicator and forms a solution of sodium sulfate. Describe how the student can obtain pure, dry crystals of hydrated sodium sulfate from the solution.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Crystals of hydrated sodium sulfate decompose when heated. This is the equation for the decomposition. $\mathrm {N a} _ {2} \mathrm {S O} _ {4}. \mathrm {x H} _ {2} \mathrm {O} \rightarrow \mathrm {N a} _ {2} \mathrm {S O} _ {4} + \mathrm {x H} _ {2} \mathrm {O}$ A student uses this apparatus to find the value of x. hydrated sodium sulfate The student heats the crystals until the decomposition is complete. The table shows the student's results. Use the results to calculate the value of x. [for $ \mathrm{N a_{2} S O_{4}} $ $ M_{\mathrm{r}}=1 4 2 $ for $ \mathrm{H_{2}O}, M_{\mathrm{r}}=1 8 $
